Beyond the blue

Most of our planet
is out of sight.

Below the waves is a vast, layered world. Each descent reveals a new way to survive.

As daylight thins and pressure rises, the familiar gives way to the unexpected. Some animals make their own light; others drift through the dark, exquisitely adapted to a world we are only beginning to understand.

The sunlit sea

Here, sunlight powers the microscopic life at the base of the marine food web. It is the ocean layer most familiar to us, full of movement, color and change.
